channel.title: CNS Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Cell, Nature, and Science.

item.title: Cell: Genome-scale perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells maps context-specific regulators of T cell programs and human immune traits
item.description: A dynamic atlas of gene regulation was generated by perturbing every expressed gene across 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells under resting conditions and following re-stimulation. The resulting map reveals context-specific regulators of immune programs and links regulatory pathways to naturally occurring T cell states and autoimmune disease risk.

item.title: Cell: Human nuclear ribomes reveal DNA-embedded ribonucleotides as epigenetic modulators of transcription-associated DNA supercoiling
item.description: Human nuclear ribomes reveal that DNA-embedded ribonucleotides accumulate at promoter-associated regulatory elements and scale with transcriptional activity. RNase H2 and Top1 process these ribonucleotides to modulate DNA supercoiling, uncovering a previously unrecognized epigenetic mechanism underlying transcription.

item.title: Science: Autism mutations rewire protein interaction networks to drive neurodevelopmental pathology
Science: Nonviral delivery of chemically modified tRNA rescues nonsense mutations in cystic fibrosis
Science: Genomic predisposition is associated with the direction of sex chromosome evolution
Science: A necroptotic-to-apoptotic signaling axis underlies inflammatory bowel disease
Science: Foreshock productivity and rupture nucleation in injection-induced earthquakes in western Canada
Science: Hierarchical sensory processing in zebrafish thalamocortical-like circuits
Science: Recovering signatures of archaic hominin introgression using ancestral recombination graphs
Science: Tunnel field-effect transistors exhibiting performance beyond the Boltzmann thermionic limit
Science: A tripartite genetic conflict system controls hybrid sterility in rice
Science: Direct evaporation of single-crystal metal contacts for 2D semiconductors
Science: Hypervision: An on-chip hyperspectral microsystem for online video-rate computational imaging
Science: High-efficiency, long-lived lead-free perovskite light-emitting diodes
Science: SGLT2 inhibitors activate pantothenate kinase in the human heart
Science: Iron-catalyzed [1+1+1] cyclopropanation by sequential coupling of an ester to two carbenes
Science: Thermal cycling–induced nitriding increases energy-storage density in titanate ferroelectric films
Science: De novo design of RNA pseudoknots with deep learning
Nature: Automated prototyping of genetic codes
item.description: A robotic, cell–free platform rapidly prototypes redesigned genetic codes, enabling the translation of proteins with reassigned codons and non-standard amino acids without altering living genomes.

item.title: Nature: Insights into longevity and virus-driven adaptation from Myotis bat genomes
item.description: Comparative and functional analyses of Myotis bats uncover unique patterns of adaptation in virus-interacting proteins and longevity-associated pathways, linking two hallmarks of bat biology.

item.title: Nature: Ultrafast and reference-free sequence discovery in single-cell data
item.description: Malva enables ultrafast, reference-free searching of raw single-cell sequences across millions of cells, transforming static transcriptomic atlases into dynamic resources for understanding the functions of sequences.

item.title: Nature: Cell-type-specific eQTLs underlie the genetic architecture of complex traits
item.description: Single-cell RNA-sequencing shows that cell-type-specific expression quantitative trait loci drive much of complex trait heritability, highlighting cell-type-specific gene regulation as key to linking genetic variants with traits.

item.title: Nature: Endocannabinoids facilitate reward engagement through retrograde gain control
item.description: A key role for retrograde neuromodulatory signalling in motivated behaviour is shown through dynamic endocannabinoid release within a thalamostriatal circuit that regulates behavioural engagement during reward seeking.

item.title: Nature: Primate-specific regulation of the human glycosphingolipid gatekeeper UGCG
item.description: Cryogenic electron microscopy structures of full-length human UGCG, the gatekeeper that dictates the scale and composition of glycosphingolipid diversity, are reported, showing that it uses a metal-independent catalytic mechanism driven by an arginine network.

item.title: Nature: Granule cells reorient cortical trajectories to separate contexts
item.description: Simultaneous imaging of premotor cortex and cerebellar granule cells in mice learning two skills in parallel shows that trajectories generalize in cortex but coherently reorient apart in granule cells, supporting generalization and separation between contexts.

item.title: Nature: Long-read sequencing reveals pre-meiotic gene conversion in sperm
item.description: Single-molecule long-read sequencing of human sperm reveals variation in recombination across donors and that a substantial fraction of non-crossover gene conversions arises before meiosis, distinct from PRDM9-driven recombination and associated with fragile sites.

item.title: Nature: Amphibious stem-insect sheds light on colonization of land
item.description: Restudy of a challenging fossil using cross-polarized light imaging and phylogenetic reconstruction identifies Chosha praecursor , a probable early-diverging insect, helping to bridge the longstanding ‘hexapod gap’ in the fossil record.

item.title: Nature: Synergistic degradation of fucoidans in the ocean
item.description: Efficient degradation of fucoidans depends on complementary bacterial guilds that cooperatively break backbone and side-chain sugars, revealing a conserved, globally relevant mechanism that shapes marine carbon cycling.

item.title: Nature: Aberrant excitatory neuronal ERBB4 promotes Alzheimer’s disease pathology
item.description: Neuroinflammation alone may be dispensable for early synapse loss in Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature: A binding-to-release strategy for targeted anticancer drug delivery
item.description: A binding-to-release drug conjugate strategy enables targeted payload release without cellular internalization, improving tumour specificity, efficacy and expanding therapeutic targets beyond conventional drug conjugates.

item.title: Cell: Integrative spatial profiling of 3D genome organization and gene expression in tissue
item.description: Spatial Hi-C-RNA simultaneously maps genome architecture and gene expression from the same tissue, revealing how spatial genome organization shapes cellular identity, development, and tumor evolution beyond what transcriptomics alone can capture.

item.title: Cell: DDIAS shields single-stranded DNA in mitosis and promotes vertebrate brain development
item.description: DDIAS is identified as a factor that protects single-stranded DNA during mitosis to maintain chromosome stability, and inactivating mutations in DDIAS are identified in a human neurodevelopmental disorder.

item.title: Cell: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits
item.description: Gut bacteria convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that distribute systemically and signal independently of free nitric oxide. These microbe-derived DNICs protect against cardiometabolic disease and fatty liver by restoring compromised metabolic signaling pathways.

item.title: Cell: Synthetic transcription factors designed by domain recombination enhance CAR T cell antitumor function
item.description: Recombining domains across an entire protein family, rather than relying on natural sequences shaped by evolution, generates synthetic “DESynR” transcription factors with enhanced function. DESynR AP-1 TFs reprogram CAR T cells into non-natural, therapeutically optimized states and outperform natural AP-1 factors in antitumor immunity.

item.title: Cell: RNA structures regulate norovirus life cycle and enable rational attenuation in vivo
item.description: Genome-wide mapping of RNA structure in murine norovirus reveals structural elements whose disruption impairs viral replication in cells and in vivo. Such structural disruptions generate a genetically stable virus that elicits protective immunity in vivo, offering a rational strategy for RNA virus vaccine design.

item.title: Nature: Increasing CO 2 levels fertilize C 4 grass production
item.description: By combining a meta-analysis of CO 2 enrichment experiments with three decades of southern African savanna observations, an increase in biomass production by C 4 grasses under rising CO 2 levels in water-limited environments is revealed.

item.title: Nature: Asymmetric prefrontal representations for leader–follower dynamics
item.description: Mice spontaneously form leader and follower roles during cooperation, and the medial prefrontal cortex encodes these role dynamics and an egocentric social value map of the partner’s position.

item.title: Nature: An Icelandic pangenome reference
item.description: Newly developed methods enable construction of Icelandic haplotypes and mapping of population-scale short reads to a pangenome by reducing reference bias and improving discovery in low-mappability regions, revealing many novel variants, including pathogenic alleles.

item.title: Nature: Psychedelics align brain activity with context
item.description: The psychedelic psilocybin reorganizes brain activity into structured, context-aligned patterns that integrate internal and external processing, providing a neural basis for the felt continuity between self and world, elucidating how the psychedelic state translates into psychological change.

item.title: Nature: Pervasive phosphorylation by phage T7 kinase disarms bacterial defences
item.description: The T7 bacteriophage deactivates bacterial defence systems through T7K phosphorylation of nearly all host and phage proteins during infection.

item.title: Nature: Wake-activated neuronal populations that regulate sleep drive
item.description: Whole-brain activity mapping, targeted cell manipulations and electrophysiology in mice identify wake-activated neuronal populations that are crucial for sleep drive and can persistently reduce daily sleep amount.

item.title: Nature: Functional role of skull lymphoid structures in CNS immunosurveillance
item.description: Functional lymphoid structures within the skull bone marrow enable central nervous system immunosurveillance and shape immune responses to brain disease.

item.title: Nature: Family genetic designs in MoBa provide insights into health and functioning
item.description: The Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study demonstrates how family-based genomic data can disentangle direct genetic effects from confounding, improving studies of health and human development.

item.title: Nature: Human brain organoids record the passage of time over multiple years
item.description: Human brain organoids were developed for over five years in culture to demonstrate that brain cells can continue to mature and record the passage of time, following human-specific endogenous programs, even outside the context of the organism.

item.title: Nature: A biased allosteric modulator is a molecular glue for β 2 AR dimerization
item.description: AP-7-168, an optimized derivative of a β-arrestin-biased negative allosteric modulator of the β 2 -adrenergic receptor (β 2 AR), functions as a molecular glue to stabilize β 2 AR homodimerization.

item.title: Cell: Mutually beneficial interactions between bacteria and Arabidopsis promote phosphorus nutrition and growth
item.description: Over 20% of root-associated bacteria promote Arabidopsis seedling growth under phosphorus (P) deficiency in a host-dependent manner. Further analyses showed that P-deficient plants secrete malate to attract Acinetobacter species to the rhizoplane, where the bacteria utilize plant-secreted nitrogen and carbon sources to fuel P mobilization that benefits both parties.

item.title: Cell: Multimodal brain cell atlas across the adult macaque lifespan
item.description: A multimodal single-nucleus atlas of 2,955,873 nuclei spanning eight macaque brain regions across the adult lifespan, including exceptionally old individuals, reveals region-specific and shared patterns of cellular vulnerability during aging. This framework provides a basis for dissecting shared and divergent molecular programs underlying primate brain aging, longevity, and neurodegeneration.

item.title: Cell: Ancient genomes reveal distinct human dispersals and social stratification in the settlement history of western Remote Oceania
item.description: The peopling of Remote Oceania involved some of humanity’s greatest expansions into the open ocean. Ancient DNA spanning the last 3,000 years from the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Tonga reveals the sources and timing of dispersals following the initial settlement and uncovers social practices of an early Fijian community that experienced recent Papuan-related gene flow.

item.title: Cell: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human
item.description: This study identifies cMAF as a key transcription factor that orchestrates the molecular crosstalk between brain perivascular macrophages and arteries, thereby sustaining cerebrovascular function in health and disease.

item.title: Cell: Polyamines buffer labile iron to suppress ferroptosis
item.description: Polyamines buffer labile iron, restraining its reactivity to suppress ferroptosis. Their depletion raises labile iron and creates synthetic lethality with GPX4 loss, revealing polyamine metabolism as an endogenous regulator of iron homeostasis.

item.title: Cell: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation
item.description: Functional profiling of ∼200,000 genomic segments from vertebrate-infecting viruses uncovers RNA elements that boost gene expression by stabilizing mRNAs and enhancing translation, revealing the diversity of TENT4-dependent mixed tailing and identifying canonical poly(A) polymerase-mediated cytoplasmic polyadenylation, together expanding our understanding of post-transcriptional regulation and RNA therapeutic design.

item.title: Nature: Rb-driven transcription limits its tumour-suppressive effects in breast cancer
item.description: CDK4/6 inhibition redirects Rb chromatin occupancy to activate oestrogen-responsive genes, counteracting its own ability to maintain therapeutic cell-cycle arrest.

item.title: Nature: Neural basis of compositional control
item.description: Behaviour of human participants in a prey-pursuit task reflects dynamic blending of goal-specific control policies, with hippocampus estimating latent states, anterior cingulate cortex orchestrating policy switches and orbitofrontal cortex supplying value-based contextualization rather than driving continuous policy updating.

item.title: Nature: Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination
item.description: Cryo-electron microscopy structures show how IS621 bridge recombinase mediates DNA excision, explaining its natural preference for insertion and informing the design of programmable bridge-editing technologies.

item.title: Nature: Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance
item.description: Substantial intraspecific variation, together with species turnover, drives coordinated shifts in drought resistance such as increased embolism resistance and wider stomatal safety margins in drier forests.

item.title: Nature: Temporal uncoupling of radial glia lineage progression in cortical organoids
item.description: RGP lineage tracing in stem-cell-derived organoids shows highly plastic proliferation and reduced clonal neuronal diversity, indicating that missing non-cell-autonomous niche cues are essential for faithful temporal control of cortical lineage progression.

item.title: Nature: Procognitive restoration of PV neuron plasticity in neurodevelopmental disorders
item.description: Expression of Meis2 in hippocampal parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in an adult mouse model of neurodevelopmental disorders rescues experience-dependent plasticity, improves memory and network function and suppresses seizures.

item.title: Nature: Maternal influences on infant gut microbiome and health
item.description: The maternal gut microbiome is a predictor of infant eczema.

item.title: Nature: In vivo genome-wide CRISPR screens of human T cells in solid tumours
item.description: An in vivo model that is able to recover human T cells from solid tumours can identify targets to help improve CAR T cell antitumour activity.

item.title: Nature: Glucose-responsive probiotics for glycaemic modulation in mice and monkeys
item.description: Engineered probiotics equipped with a synthetic glucose-responsive circuit transiently colonize the gut and secrete therapeutic factors when glucose levels increase, enabling safe, oral, sense-and-respond control of diabetes in mouse and primate models.

item.title: Nature: Luminescent-reaction-enabled super-resolution imaging
item.description: A new chemistry-based super-resolution imaging framework is described, enabling 3D, laser-free, highly sensitive and ultralong-term imaging of live cells which overcomes the limitations in spatiotemporal resolution associated with reaction-based imaging methods.

item.title: Nature: Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass
item.description: An analysis of the relationships between aboveground biomass and various climatic factors in three major regions of tropical forest shows that understanding the complex interactions between climate, topography and soils is crucial to predict how climate change will affect carbon storage capacity.

item.title: Nature: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: Potential predictive biomarkers of perioperative nivolumab therapy benefit in non-small cell lung cancer are identified from evaluable participants in the CheckMate 77T trial.

item.title: Cell: Convergent evolution of metabolic regulation governs redox adaptation in Toxoplasma
item.description: A protein called TgPRO enables the metabolic adaptation and survival of apicomplexan parasites such as Toxoplasma under oxidative and nutrient stress.

item.title: Cell: The sex and reproductive plasticity of intestinal muscles instruct gut size
item.description: Adult intestinal size plasticity is driven not only by epithelial stem cells but also by remodeling of the surrounding visceral musculature. Sex- and reproduction-dependent muscle remodeling controls gut size and transit, revealing the intestinal muscle as an active regulator of adult organ adaptation.

item.title: Cell: The structural basis for LRRK2’s activation and autoinhibition
item.description: Elevated kinase activity in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is linked to Parkinson’s disease; this study shows that its ROC GTPase acts as a nucleotide-dependent molecular switch that regulates activation and autoinhibition and reveals how some but not all PD mutations disrupt this regulatory switch.

item.title: Nature: Learning millisecond protein dynamics from what is missing in NMR spectra
Cell: Spatial biology reveals altered macrophage states in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer
item.description: Spatial multi-omics reveals macrophage states that constrain adaptive immunity in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer.

item.title: Nature: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilium mechanisms contribute to stress behaviours
item.description: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilia are disrupted during stress, and their restoration leads to improvements in stress-related behaviour in mice.

item.title: Nature: Antigen presentation by CD40 + MHC-II + astrocytes promotes CNS autoimmunity
item.description: Astrocytes promote central nervous system (CNS) immunity through antigen presentation and activation of CD40 in astrocytes by CD40L expressed by CD4 + T cells in a model of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.

item.title: Nature: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
item.description: Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a foundation model for spatial proteomics that captures tissue organization across scales, supports marker reconstruction, cell segmentation and typing, niche annotation, spatial biomarker discovery and patient stratification across heterogeneous panels and datasets.

item.title: Nature: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19
item.description: Chronic reactivation of distinct herpesviruses and anelloviruses occur during acute and long COVID-19, and track with disease severity, inflammation and outcomes, revealing immune signatures with prognostic potential.

item.title: Nature: FNIP1 variants are associated with favourable metabolism in 1 million humans
item.description: The FNIP1 pathway has a role in human energy metabolism, and its inhibition is a potential therapeutic strategy in cardiometabolic disease.

item.title: Cell: Targeting peripheral 5-HT2AR enhances antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer
item.description: By selectively targeting peripheral 5-HT2AR without inducing psychedelic effects, a non-brain-penetrant agonist boosts antitumor CD8+ T cell immunity and improves immunotherapy responses in preclinical models of colorectal cancer.

item.title: Cell: Metabolic atlas of early human cortex reveals glycolytic remodeling and pentose phosphate pathway control of cell fate transitions
item.description: The developing human cortex is composed of diverse cell types, but how nutrient metabolism shapes their fate has remained unclear. This study maps the metabolic landscape of the developing human cortex and identifies glycolysis and pentose phosphate pathway activity as key regulators of radial glia fate, controlling the generation of outer radial glia and inhibitory neurons.

item.title: Cell: Distinct cellular phenotypes of language and executive decline in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.description: Beyond its motor dimension, ALS can also involve cognitive impairment, with affected domains varying across individuals. Rather than a single common disease process, this heterogeneity reflects regionally and cellularly distinct alterations in the prefrontal cortex that are only partially predicted by TDP-43 neuropathology.

item.title: Cell: Ultrarapid deep 3D histology enables intraoperative mapping of glioma infiltration
item.description: ULTRA compresses 3D histology from days or hours to within 30 minutes by leveraging the chemical specificity of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy through the synergistic development of rapid tissue clearing and unsupervised AI. The platform enables intraoperative visualization of glioma architecture and depth-dependent tumor infiltration margins.

item.title: Cell: Milk osteopontin alters the infant microbiome to drive DC hematopoiesis and disease tolerance
item.description: Milk-derived osteopontin confers protection from viral or bacterial severe lower respiratory illness by altering the neonatal gut microbiome.

item.title: Cell: Co-option of retrotransposons promotes antibody diversification
item.description: A longstanding mystery in antibody diversification is how AID specifically targets immunoglobulin V genes. Ancient LINE-1 retrotransposons embedded within the immunoglobulin locus provide a recruitment platform for the HUSH complex and AID to drive somatic hypermutation.

item.title: Cell: Spatial atlas of the human brain vasculature reveals specialized cell ensembles
item.description: An integrative cell and spatial atlas defines the organizing logic of the adult human cerebrovasculature, providing a framework for studying how vascular cell states support brain function and shape neurological disease vulnerability.

item.title: Cell: Dietary arginine drives codon-dependent MHC class I translation and improves immunity in colon tumorigenesis and respiratory viral infection
item.description: Arginine availability regulates arginyl tRNA levels and codon-dependent translation of MHC class I, tuning antigen presentation and shaping anti-viral and anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Cell: Basement membrane turnover controls cell shape
item.description: Basement membranes are scaffolds of proteins, like collagen, that give organs shape. During development, basement membranes must adapt to the growing organ. We infer how fast the basement membrane adapts by measuring collagen turnover. We find that perlecan, another basement membrane protein, regulates collagen turnover to control organ shape.

item.title: Cell: CRISPR screens identify targets to rescue age-related T cell dysfunction in cancer
item.description: Dusp5 and Zfp219 serve as critical regulators of age-related T cell dysfunction, with the loss of either driving T cells into an effector-like state that improves tumor control through distinct mechanisms within the aged tumor microenvironment.

item.title: Cell: Gasdermin E couples viral pyroptosis to lethal hepatic lipid accumulation
item.description: Wetland virus activates dual apoptotic cascades to trigger GSDME-dependent hepatocyte pyroptosis, which rewires cellular lipid metabolism and ultimately causes severe hepatic steatosis. Therapeutic targeting of this pyroptosis-metabolism axis alleviates lethal wetland virus infection in mice.

item.title: Nature: The past and future impact of climate change on childhood malaria in Africa
item.description: Climate and econometric modelling reveal that human-induced climate change is shifting the burden of childhood malaria in Africa.

item.title: Cell: Advancing cancer detection and treatment using longitudinal routine clinical data
item.description: Liu et al. develop Oncoformer, a multimodal transformer that reads routine laboratory tests and chest X-rays already collected in everyday care. Across more than 3.6 million individuals, it detects cancer, infers tumor stage, and stratifies treatment response and recurrence risk, pointing toward risk-adapted cancer care built on data already in hand.

item.title: Cell: Dynamic dimer-of-dimers architecture defines Mg2+ transport in human CNNM4
item.description: Cryoelectron microscopy structures of human CNNM4 in distinct conformational states reveal how an unexpected dimer-of-asymmetric-dimers architecture mediates Mg2+/Na+ exchange and identify an intracellular acidic patch that may function in cellular magnesium sensing.

item.title: Cell: An Oryza orphan gene confers trans-species drought tolerance
item.description: ROAD1 is an Oryza-specific orphan gene that co-opts conserved ABA signaling to enhance drought tolerance without obvious growth defects or yield penalty under normal conditions. Elite rice lines carrying its functional allele exhibited higher grain yield than controls under drought, and its heterologous expression enhanced drought tolerance across diverse angiosperms.

item.title: Cell: Trichoderma swollenin activates AtABCB5-dependent auxin efflux to promote plant development
item.description: The beneficial fungus Trichoderma acts through the secreted swollenin ThSWO, which crosses the plant cell wall and engages AtABCB5, an auxin efflux carrier, at the host cell surface. This effector-transporter module tunes auxin-associated cellular responses, revealing how beneficial fungi co-opt host hormone transport to promote root development.

item.title: Cell: Condensates of the chromatin regulator ANKRD11 restrict hypertranscribed genes to safeguard development
item.description: ANKRD11 restricts hypertranscribed genes by forming biomolecular condensates that spatially sequester elongation factors, with disruption of this condensate-mediated control leading to aberrant organogenesis and underlying the pathogenesis of developmental disorders like KBG syndrome.

item.title: Cell: The intrinsic cardiac nervous system is essential for cardiac function and survival
item.description: Two genetically distinct neuronal subtypes in the intrinsic cardiac nervous system are differentially required for baseline cardiac function and stress resilience to maintain cardiac stability and survival.

item.title: Nature: Mapping drivers of life expectancy change in Asia from 1990 to 2023
item.description: Using the Global Burden of Disease Study data across Asian countries and territories, life expectancy trends and the effects of cause-specific mortality and risk factors on changes in these trends are analysed.

item.title: Nature: Efficient and precise programmable DNA knock-in without double-strand breaks
item.description: Kilobase-scale nickase-targeting (KNIT) editing enables single-nick-based DNA insertion across genomic loci and cell types, supporting insertion of DNA fragments exceeding 10 kb, with high efficiency and minimal unwanted off-target effects.

item.title: Nature: Genetic background sets the trajectory of experimental cancer evolution
item.description: Experimentally replaying tumour evolution in divergent mouse strains reveals the importance of interactions between genetic ancestry and acquired cancer-driving mutations in shaping the earliest stages of cancer development.

item.title: Cell: Localized PD-1 CAR T therapy reprograms neuroinflammation
item.description: PD-1+ T follicular helper-like cells drive B cell-associated pathology in multiple sclerosis. Programmable PD-1-targeting CAR T cells selectively eliminate these pathogenic CD4 T cells while delivering IL-10 at sites of inflammation, thereby suppressing neuroinflammation across preclinical models.

item.title: Cell: CSF clearance through arachnoid fenestrations to olfactory meningeal lymphatics
item.description: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) crosses arachnoid fenestrations near the olfactory bulbs to reach dural lymphatics that traverse the cribriform plate, connect to nasal lymphatics, and drain to cervical lymph nodes. Aging impairs this pathway, but intranasal VEGF-C restores the lymphatics and the CSF outflow.

item.title: Cell: A bivalent molecular glue linking lysine acetyltransferases to oncogene-induced cell death
item.description: Chemically induced proximity of lysine acetyltransferases (KATs) with BCL6 reprograms epigenetic signaling to eliminate lymphoma tumors. Structural and mechanistic studies demonstrate that fortuitous protein-protein contacts convert proximity induction into targeted changes in chromatin, revealing a key mechanism by which small molecules can co-opt oncogenic transcriptional regulators to elicit malignant cell death.

item.title: Cell: Robust regulatory interplay of enhancers, facilitators, and promoters in a native chromatin context
item.description: Using an in situ genome-rewriting platform, Zhou et al. demonstrate that precise transcriptional regulation of the NMU promoter is governed by a 3D regulatory hub comprising a core retroviral LTR enhancer, a decoy LTR promoter, and activity-boosting “facilitator” elements.

item.title: Cell: Skin-innervating glutamatergic neurons modulate aging
item.description: Within the skin, glutamatergic neurons expressing neurofilament heavy chain (Nefh) play a role in aging. Loss of Nefh during aging drives skin fibroblast senescence and collagen loss, whereas glutamate supplementation improves skin aging phenotypes.

item.title: Cell: Spatial proximity sequencing maps developmental dynamics in the germinal center
item.description: Sprox-seq enables spatial profiling of protein complexes, surface proteins, and mRNAs in intact tissues by combining proximity ligation with spatial transcriptomics. In human tonsils, Sprox-seq maps germinal center interaction networks, links CD21-CD35 complexes to proliferative programs, reveals interaction-based B cell state transitions, and directly captures B cell-follicular dendritic cell communication.

item.title: Cell: Boron-bridged GIPCs stabilize cell wall anchoring and PIN polar domains
item.description: Boron cross-links glycosylinositol phosphorylceramides (GIPCs) to physically tether the plasma membrane to the cell wall in plant cells, stabilizing PIN polar domains via direct lipid-protein interaction and enabling polar auxin transport.

item.title: Cell: Whole-transcriptome-scale isoform-resolved spatial imaging of single cells in tissues
item.description: RT&T-AMP-MERFISH enables whole-transcriptome-scale, isoform-resolved spatial imaging of single cells in intact tissues and reveals how gene programs and transcript isoform usage vary across cell types and anatomical regions in the brain.

item.title: Nature: GPC3-specific dnTGFβRII-armoured CAR T cells for hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for antitumour therapy ‘armoured’ with a dominant-negative TGFβ receptor II show enhanced efficacy and tolerable safety in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma who have developed resistance or not responded to previous treatment.

item.title: Nature: A Bayesian framework for longitudinal EHR and genetic discovery
item.description: A Bayesian generative framework that integrates longitudinal electronic health records with genetic data to identify latent disease signatures is presented.

item.title: Nature: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery
item.description: A systematic evaluation shows that contemporary humanoid robots can perform laparoscopic surgical tasks through teleoperation, highlighting both their promise and key technical challenges before clinical deployment.

item.title: Nature: Chromatin landscape and epigenetic heterogeneity of acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: An ATAC-seq-based approach is used to classify acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) into 16 epigenomic subgroups, and provides insight into the role of non-genetic mechanisms in determining pathogenesis, clinical behaviour and drug sensitivity in this disease.

item.title: Cell: Four-dimensional molecular mapping from a spatial snapshot reveals the dynamics of hair follicle organogenesis
item.description: A deep-tissue spatial transcriptomics method simultaneously captures hundreds of hair follicles spanning organogenesis in mouse skin. Ordering follicles by molecular age transforms this snapshot into a map of organogenesis in both space and time, revealing the choreography of organ assembly and how it goes awry in genetically hairless mice.

item.title: Cell: Co-option of lysosomal machinery shapes the evolution of the intracellular photosymbiosis supporting coral reefs
item.description: Corals harbor intracellular algal symbionts in specialized organelles that enable them to build diverse reef ecosystems. Corals and other cnidarians have repeatedly evolved this symbiosis through the co-option of lysosomal machinery to simultaneously support photosynthesis and extract photosynthetic products from the algae.

item.title: Cell: Recurrent patterns of TOP1-mediated neuronal genomic damage shared by major neurodegenerative disorders
item.description: Single-cell whole-genome sequencing reveals a shared pattern of excessive somatic mutations across C9ORF72 ALS, C9ORF72 FTD, and Alzheimer’s disease, dominated by 2-bp deletions. These mutations arise from aberrant topoisomerase 1 (TOP1)-mediated mutagenesis linked to oxidative DNA damage, identifying a unifying mechanism of neuronal genomic instability in neurodegeneration.

item.title: Nature: Correcting congenital myasthenia-associated acetylcholine receptor defects
item.description: Cryogenic electron microscopy, chemical biology and electrophysiology are used to determine the structures and functional consequences of representative congenital myasthenic syndrome-associated mutant receptors with and without drugs, uncovering principles of pathogenesis and providing a framework for precision therapies.

item.title: Cell: Structural basis for host membrane binding and remodeling by invading malaria parasites
item.description: Isolation and high-resolution structure of the moving junction protein complex from invading malaria parasites reveals an intricate molecular machine that bridges the host-pathogen interface and informs the de novo design of a small protein binder that inhibits parasite entry into host cells.

item.title: Cell: Reconstituting human primitive streak formation through extra-embryonic cell coordination
item.description: Tissue patterning events of early human embryo development, including an embryo-disc with primitive streak-like structures, are captured using an in vitro model where embryonic stem cells are cultured with extra-embryonic cell types.

item.title: Cell: Complete biosynthesis of the anticancer cephalotaxinone and homoerythratine
item.description: Complete biosynthetic pathways for cephalotaxinone and homoerythratine were elucidated from the endangered plant Cephalotaxus fortunei. Thirteen key enzymes were identified, including two homologous cytochrome P450 enzymes that catalyze a rare divergent oxidation process governing alkaloid scaffold diversification. Full pathway reconstitution in Nicotiana benthamiana establishes a foundation for the sustainable production of the anticancer agent homoharringtonine.
